findings.title: Customers must select pages during the authorization flow

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the temporary code to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic auth with client ID and secret. Include grant_type authorization_code, the code and redirect_uri. Expected output is a JSON body with access_token, bot_id, workspace_id and owner. Store the token pair per user.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns an access_token and bot_id, and the token is stored server-side tied to the user and workspace.

evidence.quote: Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: read content: Reading shared page titles and block content is documented for the read content capability. Title is read from the properties object of the page; block content is read through paginated block children, continued by next_cursor until has_more is false.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create a public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
In the Developer portal Build section, select Connections, choose Create new connection, enter the name, development workspace and redirect URI, select Any workspace (public) so customers in other workspaces can install it, and enable only the Read content capability. Installation scope cannot be changed later.
Fields: Installation scope: Any workspace (public integration), Capabilities: Read content only, Redirect URI: your app callback URL

Store OAuth client credentials and authorization URL securely
Copy the OAuth client ID, client secret and authorization URL from the Configuration tab into server-side environment variables. Never place them in client code or source control.
Fields: OAUTH_CLIENT_ID from Configuration tab, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET from Configuration tab, NOTION_AUTH_URL from Configuration tab

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Send a test user through the consent flow and verify the callback
Done when: The redirect URI receives a code parameter and state matches the value sent, or an error parameter is handled when the user cancels.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The token endpoint returns an access_token and bot_id, and the token is stored server-side tied to the user and workspace.

Boundary check: confirm access is limited to shared pages
Done when: A page not shared with the connection returns 404 and no content is returned.

Read a shared page title
Done when: The response object is page and the property with type title yields the page title text. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only this GET request with read content capability and no write or admin calls.

Read page content blocks
Done when: The response contains a results array of block objects for the shared page, and has_more and next_cursor are recorded for continuation. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only this block children GET with no write calls.

Continue paging through all page content blocks
Done when: Requests continue until has_more is false and all results are collected.

Continue reading page content blocks
Done when: Every page of block children has been read and the last response has has_more false. Boundary check: confirm every request in the log is a GET of the same block children endpoint with no write calls.
